adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In JS/TS object literals, computed property names like `[expr]` evaluate to a single literal string key at definition time; `z.string().toString()` does not create a “match any key” rule. So this schema will not validate arbitrary token responses as intended in sync mode (it will only recognize those specific literal keys and will not enforce/allow dynamic numeric expiry fields correctly), making `safeParse(response)` likely fail unexpectedly (or enforce bogus keys). This is a concrete correctness defect in the newly added sync-mode parsing logic.
